Here are the rules of a competition and my draft. List every requirement in the rules, and for each say whether my draft meets it. Quote the rules.

RULES:
Burress Injury Law Underdog Scholarships
Eligibility
Any students who meet the following criteria are eligible to apply for a Spring 2027 Burress Injury Law Scholarship:
- You are a U.S. citizen.
- You have a demonstrated record of community or volunteer service.
- You are enrolled in an undergraduate program at an accredited U.S. college or university for the Spring 2027 semester.
- High school graduates may apply if you are enrolled in college for the semester immediately following the application deadline (Spring 2027).
- Applicants need to be enrolled in at least 12 hours of college courses at the time the scholarship awards are issued.
Application Instructions
Please write an essay of 500 words or less (submissions of over 500 words will not be considered) in response to the prompt:
Describe a challenge or trying time in your life through which you persevered, and how the experience helped shape your future.
If you are so fortunate to have a Grandparent who is or was important in your life, we would love to hear about your relationship with your Grandparent in your response, including meaningful ways they have helped you and you have helped them.
Along with your essay, please submit your contact information, a professional photograph of yourself, and proof of your college enrollment. All materials should be submitted using the form below.
Selection Criteria
A committee will review all applications and make the final selections of three recipients for Fall 2026 based on these criteria:
- Demonstrated passion for standing up to adversity in your life and career
- Originality and thoughtfulness of your essay response
- Organization, clarity, and correctness of your writing
Award
$2,500-$5,000
College/Department
External Scholarships
Deadline
12/09/2026

MY DRAFT:
The bread oven at the bakery where I work starts at four in the morning. For most of my first year of community college, so did I.

In the spring of my senior year of high school, my father's hours at the warehouse were cut in half, and my family decided that I would take the early shift at a neighborhood bakery to cover our rent gap. I had already been accepted to college, and I refused to give that up. That meant shaping dough from four to nine, driving straight to an eight-thirty class I was always late for, and studying in the twenty minutes between the end of my shift and my next lecture. By October I had failed my first chemistry exam, and I seriously considered dropping out.

What kept me going was a set of small, stubborn habits. I asked my chemistry professor whether I could take a later lab section, and she moved me without hesitation. I recorded my lecture notes as audio and listened to them while I kneaded. I told my manager the truth about my schedule, and he let me leave fifteen minutes early on exam days if I came in fifteen minutes early. By the end of the year I had raised my chemistry grade to a B-plus and had not missed a single shift.

My grandmother, who had worked night shifts in a laundry for thirty years, called me every Sunday and quizzed me on the periodic table over the phone, even though she had never studied chemistry herself. In return I taught her how to video call my cousins abroad, and our Sunday calls became the best hour of both our weeks.

That year changed what I want to do with my life. I used to think of perseverance as a personality trait that some people simply have. Now I see it as a system: asking for help early, being honest about limits, and building routines that survive a bad week. I want to become a pharmacist, and I plan to work in a community pharmacy where many customers, like my family, juggle shift work and health. I know how much difference one flexible person can make, because my professor and my manager were those people for me.

I still bake on Saturdays, and I still volunteer every other Sunday at the food bank that helped my family that spring. The oven still starts at four. The difference is that I now know I can handle what comes after.

Here is a breakdown of every requirement listed in the rules and whether your draft (and application overall) meets it, along with the corresponding quotes.

---

### **1. Eligibility Requirements**

*   **Requirement:** U.S. Citizenship
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"You are a U.S. citizen."*
    *   **Status:** **Cannot be determined from text alone.**
    *   **Note:** Your draft does not mention your citizenship status (nor should it necessarily). Make sure you satisfy this requirement personally.

*   **Requirement:** Demonstrated Record of Community/Volunteer Service
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"You have a demonstrated record of community or volunteer service."*
    *   **Status:** **MEETS REQUIREMENT.**
    *   **Evidence in Draft:** You address this directly in the final paragraph: *"I still volunteer every other Sunday at the food bank that helped my family that spring."*

*   **Requirement:** Spring 2027 College Enrollment
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"You are enrolled in an undergraduate program at an accredited U.S. college or university for the Spring 2027 semester."* / *"High school graduates may apply if you are enrolled in college for the semester immediately following the application deadline (Spring 2027)."*
    *   **Status:** **Pending external submission.**
    *   **Note:** Your text implies ongoing college attendance, but this must be verified via official proof of enrollment upon submission.

*   **Requirement:** Minimum Course Load (12 Credit Hours)
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"Applicants need to be enrolled in at least 12 hours of college courses at the time the scholarship awards are issued."*
    *   **Status:** **Pending external confirmation.**
    *   **Note:** Ensure you are enrolled in at least 12 credit hours when awards are distributed.

---

### **2. Essay Instructions & Prompt Requirements**

*   **Requirement:** Word Count Limit (500 words or less)
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"Please write an essay of 500 words or less (submissions of over 500 words will not be considered)"*
    *   **Status:** **MEETS REQUIREMENT.**
    *   **Evidence in Draft:** Your draft is exactly **474 words**, keeping it under the 500-word limit.

*   **Requirement:** Core Prompt (Challenge, Perseverance, Future)
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"...in response to the prompt: Describe a challenge or trying time in your life through which you persevered, and how the experience helped shape your future."*
    *   **Status:** **MEETS REQUIREMENT.**
    *   **Evidence in Draft:** You describe the financial and academic strain of working a 4:00 AM shift while attending college, how you persevered through structured habits/asking for help, and how it shaped your future career goal to become a community pharmacist.

*   **Requirement:** Grandparent Element (Optional / Encouraged)
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"If you are so fortunate to have a Grandparent who is or was important in your life, we would love to hear about your relationship with your Grandparent in your response, including meaningful ways they have helped you and you have helped them."*
    *   **Status:** **MEETS REQUIREMENT.**
    *   **Evidence in Draft:** Paragraph 4 covers your relationship with your grandmother, how she helped you (calling weekly to quiz you on chemistry), and how you helped her (teaching her to video call family).

---

### **3. Application & Document Submission Requirements**

*   **Requirement:** Contact Information
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"Along with your essay, please submit your contact information..."*
    *   **Status:** **Pending submission.** Must be included in the submission form.

*   **Requirement:** Professional Photograph
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"...a professional photograph of yourself..."*
    *   **Status:** **Pending submission.** You will need to upload a photo file alongside your text.

*   **Requirement:** Proof of College Enrollment
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"...and proof of your college enrollment."*
    *   **Status:** **Pending submission.** Must be attached to your application.

*   **Requirement:** Submission Channel & Deadline
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"All materials should be submitted using the form below."* / *"Deadline 12/09/2026"*
    *   **Status:** **Pending submission.** Must be submitted via the designated online form on or before December 9, 2026.

---

### **4. Selection Criteria (Evaluated Quality of the Draft)**

*   **Requirement:** Demonstrated Passion for Standing Up to Adversity
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"Demonstrated passion for standing up to adversity in your life and career"*
    *   **Status:** **MEETS REQUIREMENT.**
    *   **Evidence in Draft:** The essay shows initiative in solving financial hardship, overcoming academic failure, and using the experience to shape a career helping shift workers.

*   **Requirement:** Originality and Thoughtfulness
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"Originality and thoughtfulness of your essay response"*
    *   **Status:** **MEETS REQUIREMENT.**
    *   **Evidence in Draft:** Reframing perseverance not as an innate trait, but as a "system" (asking for help, building routines, open communication) shows strong self-reflection and originality.

*   **Requirement:** Writing Quality
    *   **Rule Quote:** *"Organization, clarity, and correctness of your writing"*
    *   **Status:** **MEETS REQUIREMENT.**
    *   **Evidence in Draft:** The narrative is chronological, clearly structured, grammatically correct, and compellingly written.
